description: "Spec Kit traceability and automatic governance for issues and plans."
applyTo: "specs/**,plans/**,.specify/**,.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**,.github/workflows/spec-kit-governance.yml,scripts/Test-SpecKitGovernance*.ps1"
---

# Spec Kit governance

- Product behavior and cross-cutting engineering features use the Spec Kit flow:
  specification, clarification, plan, tasks, analysis, implementation, and convergence.
- Every `specs/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` and `plan.md` references an authoritative
  GitHub issue.
- Spec Kit artifacts remain in their feature directory below `specs/`.
- Standalone project, quality, refactoring, and roadmap plans belong in `plans/`.
  They declare a GitHub issue and whether Spec Kit is required, already linked,
  or not applicable.
- Delete completed standalone plans. Closed GitHub issues and Git history retain
  the durable record.
- Every issue form includes the required `Spec Kit workflow` classification.
  Issues generated by `$speckit-taskstoissues` use canonical `TNNN:` titles.
- `scripts/Test-SpecKitGovernance.ps1` is the executable policy. Keep its
  self-tests and `.github/workflows/spec-kit-governance.yml` synchronized with
  policy changes.
- Governance failures MUST be fixed at the source. Do not weaken validation,
  rename files to avoid checks, or mark Spec Kit as not applicable without a
  concrete reason.
